It is an environment with a strong presence in the Brazilian market, a sophisticated business model for monetizing digital goods and a wide availability of public documents and public statements by consumers.<1>p. 38</1>

The case plays a supporting role, not a leading one, and appears in vignettes when a category needs to be stabilized or when it must be shown how the formal rule becomes enforcement practice. This use is kept in check by distinguishing three layers of normativity. The declared layer lies in the terms, policies and announcements. The layer in operation lies in the technical architecture, the interface flows and the concrete forms of enforcement and sanction, and it is there that the promise takes shape and much of the informational asymmetry is produced.
In the work as a whole, the selected ecosystem plays a supporting role, not a leading one.<1>p. 58</1>

Recourse to the case is limited and instrumental, because it serves to anchor inferences and to make concrete certain mechanisms whose abstract formulation might sound overly generic. For this reason, references to the ecosystem will be used as vignettes and points of support, invoked only when needed to stabilize the meaning of a category, illustrate a typical governance arrangement or show how a formal rule turns into enforcement practice.<1>p. 57</1>

First, there is a declared normativity, in the form of terms, policies, rules and institutional announcements, through which the platform describes the service, defines conditions of access, establishes rights and duties and announces, when it chooses to, the limits of the promised experience.<1>p. 58</1>

Second, there is a normativity in operation, which is not confined to the formal text and shows itself in the technical architecture, interface flows, enforcement routines, mechanisms for modulating the experience and concrete forms of enforcement and sanction. This layer is decisive, because it is there that the contractual promise takes shape, and it is also there that a significant part of the informational asymmetry typical of continuous digital consumption is produced.<1>p. 58</1>

The disputed layer arises when the first two clash, because enforcement reveals what the text left unclear, because the text serves as an alibi or because a unilateral change shifts the balance without the consumer knowing what was altered. Keeping them apart prevents confusing statement with enforcement, promise with delivery and controversy with mechanism. The case has limits. The design focuses on this ecosystem, in its computer and mobile versions (the latter called Wild Rift), within a defined time frame and using public sources, and this choice neither maps variations by platform, national market or technological generation nor supports statistical inference. The reflection, therefore, is not about League of Legends as an isolated cultural object but about the regime of the immaterial object of consumption it contains.

There is, further, a disputed normativity, which emerges when the two previous layers clash, whether because enforcement reveals consequences the text did not make clear, because the text serves as an alibi for practices perceived as abusive, or because unilateral changes shift the balance of the service without the consumer being able to recognize precisely what was altered and with what effects.<1>p. 58</1>

Delimiting these arenas is not a classificatory whim but a way of keeping the analysis from confusing statement with enforcement, promise with delivery or controversy with mechanism, while ensuring that each step of the argument rests on the appropriate layer of the phenomenon examined.<1>p. 58</1>

The methodological design focuses on a paradigmatic case, the Riot Games ecosystem with League of Legends, in its desktop and mobile (“Wild Rift”) versions, within a defined time frame and relying on public and documentary sources, so as to build a verifiable corpus. This choice limits the mapping of variations by type of platform, national market and technological generation, and is not aimed at producing statistical inferences from a representative sample.<1>p. 78-79</1>

The work's potential for generalization derives, first, from what the instrumental empirical laboratory makes observable, not from anything “typical” or “individual” about the case, yielding analytical generalization through mechanisms and relevant frictions. For this reason, this work does not offer a reflection on League of Legends as an isolated cultural object, but on the regime of the immaterial object of consumption it contains and on the techniques of private governance used by the continuous digital services that sustain it, reconstructed with the help of an ecosystem that clearly exposes dependence, modulation of access, internal sanctions, an economy of virtual items and the semiotic management of enjoyment.<1>p. 79</1>
What weight does each type of information carry?

Each piece of information carries a graded weight. General knowledge widespread in the sector serves only to situate the reader and proves no specific occurrence. Auxiliary technical and operational descriptions name structures and explain the vocabulary of the field. Normatively relevant statements, such as promises, powers of modulation, sanction criteria, appeal procedures and restoration parameters, require traceable and attributable sources when they serve as a premise of legal qualification, with priority given to the supplier's primary documentation.

To keep documentation effort proportionate to argumentative weight, the work distinguishes three layers of information. The first consists of general knowledge widely shared in the sector, used only to situate the reader and make the logic of continuous digital services intelligible, without claiming to prove any specific occurrence.<1>p. 60</1>

The second consists of auxiliary technical and operational descriptions, used to name internal structures and to understand the vocabulary of the field, relying subsidiarily on collaborative repositories when indispensable.<1>p. 60</1>

The third consists of normatively relevant statements, such as institutional promises, powers of modulation, sanction criteria, appeal procedures and restoration parameters, which are supported, whenever used as a premise of legal qualification, by traceable and attributable sources, with priority given to the supplier's primary documentation and verifiable public records.<1>p. 60</1>

Following Umberto Eco, the sources that make up the observed institutional world or the law in force, such as terms of use, policies, announcements, interface records, legal documents and court decisions, are kept separate from the critical literature that comments on them. The separation prevents commentary from being taken as evidence of what the platform declared or did, and prevents indirect reading from replacing primary material when the argument depends on imputation. Doctrinal analysis is not an empirical source. It works as a lens that organizes what counts as evidence, and the rule is triangulation, not exhaustiveness.

Sources are the materials that directly make up the observed institutional world or the law in force that applies to it, such as terms of use, internal policies, supplier announcements, interface records, legal documents and accessible court decisions. Critical literature is the body of texts that comment on, interpret, systematize or contest these materials, such as legal scholarship, academic articles and third-party analyses. The distinction is not formalism, since it prevents commentary from being treated as evidence of what the platform declared or did, and also prevents indirect reading from replacing contact with primary material when the argument depends on doctrinal imputation.<1>p. 50</1>

Doctrinal and bibliographic analysis, in turn, is treated not as an “empirical source” but as an interpretive lens that organizes what counts as evidence, what counts as a promise and what counts as relevant loss in the regime of the Immaterial Object of Consumption.<1>p. 61</1>
The general rule is to work by triangulation and by the sufficiency of the core of evidence relevant to the argument, rather than to pursue exhaustiveness or representativeness.<1>p. 60</1>

These rules are tied to imputation, and so they also serve those who will litigate. Legal imputation depends on traceable elements whenever the argument turns on them. When the argument requires institutional attribution, such as an internal rule, a sanction criterion or a binding promise, it must rest on attributable sources, with public narratives serving only as a starting point. For public content that may change, traceability is ensured by recording at least the item identifier, the address and the date of access. The chapter on evidence carries this discipline into litigation.

When the text relies on descriptions of how things work that are widely shared in the sector, they serve as context and not as proof of a specific occurrence, and legal imputation remains dependent on traceable elements whenever the argument turns on them.<1>p. 59</1>

When, however, the argument depends on a specific institutional attribution, such as the content of an internal rule, a sanction criterion, a binding promise or a restoration procedure, it must rest on traceable and attributable sources, with public narratives used only as a starting point for locating verifiable elements.<1>p. 67</1>

For public content subject to change, traceability is ensured by recording at least the item identifier, the source address and the date of access, without any claim to build an exhaustive repository of full captures.<1>p. 61</1>
What can each source prove, and what can it not?

Situated institutional observation makes the norm in operation visible. It is neither ethnography nor personal testimony offered as proof, but observation of the platform as a working institution, in which interface, flows and communications are institutional texts that distribute understanding unequally. System messages, warnings, notifications and mechanisms of restriction, sanction and appeal count as primary evidence when described in a traceable way. The technique describes patterns and mechanisms, without measuring statistical prevalence and without inferring the supplier's psychological intentions.

This is neither community ethnography nor an account of personal experience offered as proof. The procedure is used to observe the platform as a working institution, that is, the mechanisms through which the offer is organized, the experience is steered and the relationship is performed through technical artifacts, interface flows and instruments of sanction.<1>p. 62</1>

Interface, flows and institutional communications are treated as institutional texts that organize meanings and distribute understanding unequally, shaping promises, expectations and modes of delivery. The focus is on institutionally relevant elements observable during enjoyment, such as access and configuration flows, system messages, warnings and notifications, as well as mechanisms of restriction, sanction and appeal presented to the user, used selectively when needed to stabilize the description of the mechanism under discussion.<1>p. 62</1>

The elements observed are treated as primary evidence when they can be described in a traceable way, preserving, where relevant, the minimum context in which they occurred and what is needed to allow what was described to be verified.<1>p. 62</1>

The procedure aims to describe verifiable institutional patterns and mechanisms, without claiming to measure the statistical prevalence of individual experiences or to infer the supplier's psychological intentions.<1>p. 63</1>

Documentary analysis captures the declared norm, the repertoire of promises, duties, unilateral powers and procedures that the supplier presents as a condition of use, and these documents help shape the content of what is supplied over time. Terms of use, licenses and penalty and conduct policies form the primary normative core. Help pages, FAQs and announcements have a complementary status and do not replace the core when formal powers, sanctions or risk are at issue. Documents do not, by themselves, prove how the rules are applied day to day.

The documents actually used in the text are selected for their relevance to the problem investigated, and their function is to capture the declared norm of the ecosystem, that is, the repertoire of promises, duties, unilateral powers and enforcement procedures presented as a condition of access and use. In platform-governed objects, such documents are not mere informational accessories, since they help shape the content of what is supplied over time and delimit, explicitly or implicitly, the range of permitted modulations, the sanction regimes and the mechanisms of appeal and restoration.<1>p. 63-64</1>

Terms of use, licenses and penalty and conduct policies are taken as the primary normative core of the governance regime, because they structure powers, duties and consequences. Support materials, help pages and official announcements are given a complementary status, capable of showing public promises, declared procedures and the justifications offered to the user, without replacing the normative core when the analysis turns on definitions of formal powers, sanction regimes or risk allocation.<1>p. 65</1>

The procedure aims to delimit, traceably, the declared institutional design of the ecosystem, without claiming that documents, by themselves, prove how the rules are concretely applied day to day.<1>p. 66</1>

Public statements by users, in videos and on complaint platforms, are a symptomatic record of recurring frictions, useful for mapping conflicts and vocabularies and for guiding triangulation with the declared norm and the norm in operation. They neither prove institutional conduct nor establish, by themselves, internal policies, decision criteria or obligations undertaken. Forums such as Reddit cannot be used to infer representativeness or prevalence, and collaborative repositories such as Fandom serve only to name categories and describe mechanics.
Users' accounts of their experience and their interpretations do not serve as an autonomous evidentiary basis.<1>p. 62</1>
The survey of public user statements is part of the empirical collection for a limited and subsidiary purpose, as a symptomatic record of recurring frictions in the ecosystem.<1>p. 66</1>

The selection of public statements focuses on two main arenas, chosen because they serve as recurring channels for airing conflicts in the ecosystem: YouTube, as a space for accounts and controversies in audiovisual form, and structured complaint platforms that record consumer conflicts in the user's own words under thematic classification.<1>p. 67</1>

This material is used neither as autonomous proof of the supplier's institutional conduct nor as a substitute for official documents, interface records, lawsuits or decisions. It serves to map recurring frictions, identify relevant vocabularies and discursive patterns and guide triangulation with the declared norm and the norm in operation, under minimum selection and recording criteria that allow the material actually cited to be verified externally.<1>p. 66</1>

Community and platform sources, such as forums, social networks, collaborative repositories and creator content, are given a limited and subsidiary methodological function. They are not used to establish, by themselves, the content of the supplier's internal policies, its decision criteria, its moderation procedures or the existence of obligations undertaken, nor to assert that disputed institutional practices occurred.<1>p. 67</1>

For this reason, Reddit is used in a referenced way, preferably through mentions and links found in videos or in documents already included, to avoid endless drift across the field. It is not used to infer how representative opinions are or how prevalent events are, but to locate threads, reference terms and verifiable leads when the ecosystem's public environment makes them relevant.<1>p. 69</1>

To make terms, internal structures and the vocabulary of the field more intelligible in technical and operational terms, and only as a complement to official sources, collaborative repositories such as Fandom are used subsidiarily. This material serves the strict purpose of naming categories of the ecosystem, describing mechanics operationally and helping to reconstruct basic relations between elements of the service when this is indispensable to translate how it works into legally intelligible language.<1>p. 69</1>
How should the platform's terms of use and policies be read?

Terms of use and policies are not a static declaration of will but parts of a governance apparatus that combines rule, implementation and continuous enforcement, with the promise recalibrated through interface, rewards, scarcity and sanctions. The contract remains legally central, because it is where licenses, access limits, unilateral powers and modulation clauses are set out. The reading connects these documents to how the service actually works in order to make the case decidable.

The institutional reading of the contract in this work starts from the recognition that terms of use and internal policies do not operate as static instruments for declaring will, but as parts of a governance apparatus that combines rule, implementation and continuous enforcement. In platform-governed ecosystems, the relevant promise is not exhausted by the contractual text, because it is reiterated and recalibrated through interface, reward routines, scarcity regimes and private sanctions.<1>p. 70</1>

Even so, the contract remains legally central, since it is where the licenses, access limits, unilateral powers and modulation clauses that sustain the enclosure and administration of the relationship are set out. The procedure adopted consists in linking the formal documents to evidence of how the institution works, in order to bring the case back to the categories of the regime of the Immaterial Object of Consumption and make it legally decidable.<1>p. 70</1>

The reading is not a full exegesis but a targeted extraction along four axes, namely how the object and the performance are qualified, the powers of unilateral modification and their triggers, the justification and allocation of risk, and the promises of compensation, refund and restoration. It also looks for the sanctions and appeal channels that exist and the duties of information that apply when something is altered, punished or restricted. For software, the period of technical validity, update cycles, discontinuation and support are included. The version in force is read and preserved as captured, and an earlier version is read only when there is a verifiable public record of it.

Instead of a full exegesis of each document, normatively relevant elements are extracted in a targeted way to reconstruct, over the life of the relationship, (i) how the object and the performance are qualified, (ii) the powers of unilateral modification and their triggers, (iii) the forms of institutional justification and risk allocation, and (iv) the promises of compensation, refund and restoration.<1>p. 64</1>

The aim, accordingly, is to identify how the service is described and promised, how access is structured and conditioned, what limits on use are set, what rules of conduct organize membership, what sanction and restriction mechanisms are provided for, what appeal and review channels are offered, what refund and restoration regimes are declared and what duties of information are provided for when something is altered, punished or restricted.<1>p. 64-65</1>

In the case of a computer program, the documentary extraction will also be targeted, looking for (i) references to the period of technical validity of the version marketed, update cycles, discontinuation milestones and conditions of withdrawal from circulation; and (ii) the design and effectiveness of the channels for support, maintenance and complementary technical services.<1>p. 65</1>

The documents actually used are collected and preserved as they appeared at the moment of capture, with a record of context and minimum traceability metadata, so that what was declared in the version used can be reconstructed.<1>p. 65</1>

As a rule, the contractual analysis takes as its reference the versions in force and accessible when the writing was completed (March 2026), considering earlier changes only occasionally, when there is a verifiable public record and when this is needed to qualify a legally relevant modulation of the relationship.<1>p. 71</1>

The reading brings together three levels. The documentary and normative level shows how the platform qualifies the object, reserves powers and promises compensation. The technical and semiological level shows how interface, metrics, visibility and rewards turn signs into value and discipline. The public experiential level shows recurring frictions and perceptions of loss. Interfaces, statements and marketing are read through semiotic vulnerability, and contracts and court decisions through the IOC, abusive teleology, open auditability and functional value equivalence.

First, an internal documentary-normative level, made up of terms of use, policies and official support documents, which shows how the platform qualifies the object, defines licenses and enclosures, reserves unilateral powers and presents justifications and promises of compensation. Second, a technical-semiological level, which shows how interface, metrics, visibility regimes and reward systems turn signs into value and everyday discipline, producing dependencies and operational expectations. Third, a public experiential level, drawn from open statements, which shows recurring patterns of friction, perceived loss and appeals to institutional promises and procedures.<1>p. 71</1>

Public statements, observation of interfaces and marketing materials are read in light of semiotic vulnerability and of mechanisms of anticipation and steering through signs, so as to make clear how belonging, reputation, time and recognition form part of the promise and the value of what is acquired. Contractual documents and court decisions are read in light of the qualification of the IOC as an immaterial product in a consumer relationship, of abusive teleology as a criterion for controlling architecture and governance, and of the parameters of open auditability and functional value equivalence as keys for dealing with opacity and mutability without neutralizing protection.<1>p. 71</1>

The complexity of the contract is neither a moral defect nor a virtue but a legal sign of a regime that concentrates decision-making power, disperses information and shifts the conflict to enforcement. Posner, Eggleston and Zeckhauser are used instrumentally, for a perspective that allows the form of the contract to be treated as evidence of the institutional environment in which it operates. For Macaulay, contracts often work as self-planning, invoked only as a last resort, which counsels giving priority to the factual situation. None of this replaces the CDC. Review remains doctrinal and protective, with the contract read as a governance interface and not as a complete snapshot of the relationship.

In continuous digital services, complexity is not just length of text. It signals that normativity is distributed across layers, with reserved powers, sanction patterns and restoration mechanisms becoming part of the very infrastructure of what is acquired.<1>p. 72</1>

Complexity is treated here neither as a moral defect of the contract nor as a virtue in itself. It is treated as a legal sign of a supply regime that concentrates decision-making power, disperses information, hinders comparison and shifts the conflict to the continuous performance of the relationship.<1>p. 72</1>

Within this frame, the reference to Posner, Eggleston and Zeckhauser is strictly instrumental. Their perspective allows the form of the contract to be treated as evidence of the institutional environment in which it raises interpretive questions about essential content, legitimate expectations and typical zones of abusiveness in standardized, unilaterally structured contracts <1>Zeckhauser</1><2>(Posner; Eggleston; Zeckhauser, 2000, p. 92)</2>.<3>p. 72</3>

In line with this caution, Macaulay shows that contracts, in many situations, work less as an ordinary mechanism for resolving disputes than as a tool for self-planning, typically invoked only as a last resort <1>Macaulay</1><2>(Macaulay, 1963, p. 55)</2>. For interpretive purposes, this counsels giving priority to the factual situation and the conflict actually expressed, rather than assuming that the text fully describes the relationship and its concrete expectations <3>Macaulay</3><4>(Macaulay, 1963, p. 61)</4>.<5>p. 73</5>

Under this perspective, contractual complexity serves as a roadmap for qualifying the relationship, guiding the identification of zones of informational asymmetry, possible structural advantages and external factors relevant to how the contract works in practice, especially when the logic governing the use of these instruments is set unilaterally by hegemonic actors <1>Zeckhauser</1><2>(Posner; Eggleston; Zeckhauser, 2000, p. 92)</2>. This key does not replace the doctrinal parameters of the Consumer Protection Code but acts as a methodological bridge that allows the phenomenon to be described rigorously enough to support the theoretical reconstruction and the doctrinal conversion of the regime. This caveat does not change the standard of review, which remains doctrinal and protective, but describes a practical condition for reading contracts that function as a governance interface and not as a complete snapshot of the relationship.<3>p. 72-73</3>
What is object and what is instrument?

Authors from political economy, sociology, philosophy and communication appear in several chapters on a precise condition. In platform economies, power tends to disguise itself as technical administration, and the risk is letting the appearance of neutrality take the place of analyzing how private decisions produce practical norms. The methodology openly takes a position and treats the regime of the service as a coupling of clauses, interface and institutional practices.

In platform economies, power tends to disguise itself as technical administration while it concentrates knowledge, organizes attention and redefines the conditions of participation. With an object of this kind, the central methodological risk is letting the apparent neutrality of how things work take the place of analyzing how private decisions produce practical norms and distribute asymmetries.<1>p. 45</1>

The methodology is a stance toward the kind of power observed in platform economies and, therefore, toward the kind of temptation such an object creates for the researcher. In environments where private administration and the management of conduct present themselves as technical neutrality, the central analytical risk is to naturalize decisions as if they were simply “how things work”, to reduce institutional choices to “operational details” and to attribute to the user, as autonomy, responses already induced by design, communication and mechanisms of incentive, disincentive and sanction. The methodological design therefore assumes as a premise that the regime under which the service actually operates emerges from the coupling of clauses, interface and institutional practices, which rules out readings that artificially separate norm, technique and culture.<1>p. 45</1>

The distinction between object and instruments comes from Umberto Eco. The object is the regime of platform-governed enjoyment, with its mechanisms of promise, expectation, modulation and sanction, and it is a real phenomenon, not a book. The instruments are the conceptual keys that translate it into language to which legal norms can apply, compatible with duties, limits and legal consequences. Frameworks from other fields are used to identify mechanisms and discipline inferences, without exegesis of the works, which guards against both exegetical drift and the ornamental use of concepts.

The object is the regime of platform-governed enjoyment and its mechanisms of promise, expectation, modulation and sanction. The instruments are the conceptual keys used to qualify this regime in language to which legal norms can apply, making it possible to convert phenomena of architecture, communication and technical enforcement into operational categories compatible with duties, limits and legal consequences.<1>p. 46</1>
“A thesis studies an object using certain instruments. Often the object is a book and the instruments are other books.<1>p. 46</1>

In other cases, on the contrary, the object is a real phenomenon; this is what happens with theses on internal migratory movements in present-day Italy, on the behavior of a group of disabled children or on the opinions of the public regarding a television program currently being broadcast.” <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 69)</2>.<3>p. 46</3>

In practical terms, frameworks from political economy, sociology, philosophy, the anthropology of consumption and communication theory come in to guide the identification of relevant mechanisms and discipline inferences, without requiring an exegetical reconstruction of the works used, so that the argument can still be traced back to verifiable evidence and recognizable normative parameters <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 69-70)</2>. This distinction aims to prevent both exegetical drift and the merely ornamental use of concepts.<3>p. 46-47</3>

The non-exegetical approach is a deliberate narrowing of focus, not a shortcut. When a concept is used to read an object other than the one in which it arose, what matters is what it makes visible, and its genealogy becomes a topic only when needed to prevent distortion. Eco gives the example of the American avant-garde of the 1950s that appropriated Zen, where what matters is what it made of Zen and not what Zen originally was. So when a chapter turns to a philosopher or an economist, it does so to qualify the phenomenon, and the legal argument can still be traced back to evidence and normative parameters.

In this sense, the choice of a non-exegetical approach is not a shortcut but a deliberate narrowing of focus. When a concept is used as a tool to read an object other than the one in which it was formed, the interest lies in what it reveals in the field observed and in how it makes the problem more legally intelligible, without requiring a philological reconstruction of its origin, internal debates and historical variants in its home domain, except where indispensable to avoid significant distortion.<1>p. 47</1>

Eco offers an explicit formulation to justify approaches that seek not a full philological reconstruction of a body of thought at its origin but an examination of its uses and appropriations in another context, provided the aim is clearly delimited.<1>p. 47</1>
Suppose, however, that while examining the critical literature I became interested in the use a certain American literary and artistic avant-garde made of Zen in the 1950s.<1>p. 47</1>

Assuming, of course, that I do not intend to show that the Californians misunderstood the original Zen, which would make comparison with the Japanese texts mandatory. But if I simply assume that they drew freely on translations from the Japanese, what interests me is what they made of Zen and not what Zen was in its origins.” <1>Eco</1><2>(Eco, 2007, p. 70-71)</2>.<3>p. 47</3>

The roles are ranked. The instruments direct attention, the sources support what is asserted, and the critical literature qualifies debates without replacing the documentary basis. The researcher's experience guides the selection of material but is not a criterion of proof.

This preserves a disciplined hierarchy. The conceptual instruments direct attention and help frame sharper questions. The sources support what can be asserted about the promises, powers, procedures and effects of the regime observed. The critical literature qualifies debates, tests readings and makes interpretive choices explicit, without replacing the documentary basis that supports the reconstruction.<1>p. 50</1>

Because the researcher is embedded in the field, experience serves as a vantage point for observation and interpretation that guides the selection and reading of the material, but not as a criterion of proof.<1>p. 49</1>
How are the chapters organized?

The reconstruction moves in three stages. It describes the regime that administers access to the digital good, its continuity and its meaning, stabilizes categories of qualification, proof and imputation under the CDC, reconciled with intellectual property, and tests these keys in illustrative applications. The theoretical framework is organized by functional axes rather than by authors, namely technique and infrastructure, culture and communication, political economy and extraction, and semiotics and platform governance.

Legal control of these ecosystems depends on a vocabulary capable of making nameable, demonstrable and imputable the decisions that now hide behind technical functioning. For this reason, the work is organized in linked movements, through which it describes the governance regime that administers access to the digital good, its continuity and its meaning, stabilizes categories of qualification, proof and imputation under the Consumer Protection Code, reconciled with the legislation underlying intellectual property rights, and, finally, tests these keys in illustrative applications drawn from typical cases of continuous digital consumption, in which unilateral reconfigurations and platform sanctions shift what counts as delivery, alter enjoyment and redistribute losses.<1>p. 30</1>

The theoretical scope functions as a grid of observation and control designed to guide the reading of the empirical material and to discipline inferences. Instead of operating as an inventory of authors, it is organized by functional axes, each associated with research questions and reading criteria.<1>p. 53</1>

A first axis treats technique and infrastructure as a form of rationality that structures possibilities of action and interpretation. A second axis treats the cultural and communicational dimension as a condition for the formation of expectations, promises and intelligibility in interface-mediated environments, also mobilizing, in a structural key, contributions from the anthropology of consumption to describe how goods, belonging and routines stabilize meanings and coordinate conduct.<1>p. 53</1>

A third axis reconstructs political economy and extraction to situate dependencies, tolls and forms of capture associated with the operation of the ecosystem. A fourth axis describes the semiotic dimension as a material component of value and as a condition of legal cognizability of the conflict, including the notion of regimes of value and of socially administered mutability of the object over time.<1>p. 53</1>
A fifth axis reconstructs platform governance as the exercise of private power through internal rules and sanction mechanisms.<1>p. 53-54</1>
